title: Enforcement ledger
subtitle: One stream per team · pure apply · preview, then commit

sections.title: One ledger per team
sections.body:
> **What a team can do is the sum of the decisions still in force. A decision is never edited; only a later one can end it.**

At any moment we can answer: **why can't this team send, who decided that, and what would change it?**

```
            append(event, seenVersion)                    read
 detector ─┐                         ┌──────────────┐
 reviewer ─┼──► preview ──► commit ──► ledger        │   Enforcement (cases)  ──► review queue, team page
 script   ─┘    (pure apply,  (same    │ team t1      │──► SendingDomain.disabled ──► send path (unchanged)
                 no write)    apply,   │ v1 opened    │   scorecard, dashboard  ──► replayed on demand
                              +version │ v2 opened    │
                              check)   │ v3 released  │
                                       └──────────────┘
                                 insert-only · one version counter per team
```

Three moving parts:
1. **The ledger**: one insert-only table, one ordered stream per team.
2. **apply(state, event)**: a pure function. Same events in, same state out, always.
3. **Projections**: the current cases, `disabled`, the queue. Updated in the same transaction as the event; rebuildable by replaying.

sections.title: Principles that fall out
sections.body:
| # | Principle | Made true by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The ledger is the only truth; everything else is computed from it | projections are written only by `append()`; nightly replay compares |
| 2 | The past is never edited; corrections are new events | `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE OR TRUNCATE` trigger raises |
| 3 | A team's events have one order | `UNIQUE (teamId, version)` |
| 4 | Every event says who and why | `num_nonnulls(actorUserId, actorRule) = 1`; a person writes a non-blank note; reason in the zod payload |
| 5 | Nothing changes what a team can do except an event | the only writer of `disabled` is `append()` |
| 6 | Events act on cases, not targets | `released` names one `caseId`; nothing releases "the domain" |
| 7 | Detectors open cases; only people close them | `released`, `upheld`, `allowed` require `actorUserId` |
| 8 | Evidence explains, never decides | evidence is in the payload; `apply` never reads it |
| 9 | New cases are new event types, not columns | `type` + `data jsonb`; one zod schema + one `apply` case per type |
| 10 | Any past moment is a query | fold up to time T; `apply` never reads the clock |
| 11 | What you preview is what you commit | preview and commit run the same `apply` on the same version |

sections.title: Implications
sections.body:
What becomes possible once every change is an event, folded by a pure function:

**For reviewers**
- **Preview before commit.** "Reenable" shows *mail.acme stays disabled: team-wide phishing case* before the click, not after.
- **No silent overwrites.** Two reviewers on one team: the second save fails with what changed, and re-previews.
- **The whole thread survives.** Upheld by Dana → released by Sam, overriding, with both notes. Today the second save rewrites the first.
- **The queue can't go stale.** It's a projection written in the same transaction as the decision.

**For the system**
- **Bugs announce themselves.** Replay ≠ projection means something wrote outside `append()`, and the replay names the team and version.
- **Fixes to the fold are testable on history.** Replay every stream with the new `apply`, diff the projections, before shipping.
- **Policy dry-runs, once inputs are kept.** Replaying events alone can't re-decide an `opened`; with the detector's inputs archived beside each opening, a candidate threshold can be run over last quarter and its openings counted before it ships.
- **Shadow detectors.** A new detector appends `proposed` events the fold ignores for `disabled`. You get its precision against reviewers' real decisions before it can block anyone.

**For senders and support**
- **The API and banner read the projection.** "Can't send: complaint rate over 24h (Oct 28)" comes from the case's reason, not from guessing (LOO-6235/6236).
- **Notifications are a subscriber.** "Notify the team when a case opens or closes" reads new events in order (LOO-6237). Versions make it resumable; exactly-once needs an outbox with an idempotency key per event.
- **Appeals have a record.** What we decided, when, and on what — at the time, not reconstructed.

**For measurement**
- **Scorecard per rule.** For each detector-opened case, what closed it and why: `review.wrong` counts against the finding, `review.too_broad` against the remedy.
- **Time to review, reversal rate, re-offense rate.** All folds over the ledger; history is complete from day one.

sections.title: Costs and risks
sections.body:
| Risk | Why it matters | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| A writer bypasses `append()` | the guarantees hold only if `append()` is the only writer of `disabled` | move every writer (the path); nightly replay finds drift; then a DB guard on `disabled` |
| `apply` changes meaning | replay would change the past | change `apply` only by adding cases; a new meaning is a new event type |
| Payload drift | old events must keep parsing | fields only added, optional, with defaults in `apply` |
| Notes may hold personal data | append-only can't erase | open decision: notes in a side table keyed by event id, redactable without touching the ledger |
| Team deletion | an FK cascade would delete the ledger, and the trigger forbids it | the ledger outlives the team: no cascade; enforcement history survives re-signup |
| Write contention | one counter per team | dozens of events per team, ever; a conflict is a retry |
| Projection and ledger disagree after a failed write | — | they can't: one transaction |
| Effects outside the database (SES tenant, emails) | a crash after commit loses them | today's behavior too; an outbox per event makes them durable (later) |
| A detector inserts a review event directly | app validation is bypassed | CHECK: only `opened` may have a rule as actor |

sections.title: The ledger and apply
Preview, then commit
sections.body:
```
preview({ teamId, events })
  state  = load projection             (version 12)
  after  = events.reduce(apply, state)
  return { basedOn: 12, changes: diff(state, after), afterCommit: [side effects] }      -- writes nothing

commit({ teamId, events, seenVersion: 12 })
  BEGIN
    lock the team's stream             (advisory lock; domain creation takes it too)
    version first, then cases, then domains
    adopt: a disabled domain with no case gets legacy.unrecorded, before anything else
    validate events against state      (case open? actor allowed? payload parses?)
    INSERT events at versions 13, 14 … -- unique (teamId, version): someone else got 13 → ROLLBACK, Conflict{since}
    after = events.reduce(apply, state)
    write changed Enforcement rows + SendingDomain.disabled
  COMMIT
  then run side effects (SES tenant, notifications)
```

- A person's conflict always goes back through a fresh preview, showing what arrived. A detector retries.
- Property test: for any event list, `preview(...).after` equals the state read back after `commit(...)`.

sections.title: The panel today
sections.body:
```
Domain review › mail.acme-example.com                  (disabled)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Suspicious activity · notices · disabled emails                  │
│                                                                  │
│ Decision ( ) BlockDomain ( ) Reenable ( ) Unleash (●) Pending    │
│ Assessment [                                              ]      │
│                                              [Save Assessment]   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

What Save does today (`saveDomainAssessment`):
- rewrites **every** Pending `DisableDomainEvent` on the team to the decision (`updateMany`)
- the assessment text lives only in `AdminPanelInteraction`, stitched back by `getAssessments`
- **Reenable** sets `disabled = false`, whatever caused it
- **Unleash** also sets `Team.skipSafetyChecks = true`, forever
- **BlockDomain** sets `disabled = true` and disables the SES tenant
- nothing says *why* the domain was disabled

sections.title: The same panel on the ledger
sections.body:
```
Domain review › mail.acme-example.com              can't send · 2 reasons
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ① Complaint rate 0.41% over 24h    health@3   Oct 28 15:52  new  │
│ ① Team-wide: possible phishing      ai@14      Oct 28 14:07  ✓ Dana│
│ ② Oct 28 16:10 Dana upheld phishing — "fake bank login page"     │
│                                                                  │
│ Decision ( ) BlockDomain (●) Reenable ( ) Unleash ( ) Pending    │
│ Assessment [ their own reset email, complaint spike was a test ] │
│ ③ Preview (v12):                                                 │
│    · Complaint rate case       open → released (review.wrong)    │
│    · mail.acme-example.com     stays disabled: team-wide phishing│
│    · queue                     acme leaves the queue             │
│                                              [Save Assessment]   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| | reads / writes |
|---|---|
| ① | open `Enforcement` rows for this domain + team-wide ones; reason text from the registry; `new` = not yet upheld |
| ② | the case's events, in order, with notes |
| ③ | `preview()` of the chosen decision against version 12; Save sends `seenVersion: 12` |

The four buttons stay:

| Button | Appends, one per open case on the domain | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Reenable | `released {review.wrong}` | re-enables only if nothing else blocks; the preview says so |
| BlockDomain | `upheld` | stays blocked, leaves the queue; SES tenant disabled after commit |
| Unleash | `released` + (later) `allowed {team, until}` | v1 keeps setting `skipSafetyChecks`; later it's a projection of an expiring exception |
| Pending | `commented` | note on the record, stays in the queue |

sections.title: When someone got there first
sections.body:
```
Domain review › mail.acme-example.com
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▲ Changed while you were reading (v12 → v13)                     │
│   Sam released "Team-wide: possible phishing" 40s ago:           │
│   "confirmed with them on support, it's their login page"        │
│                                                                  │
│ Preview (v13):                                                   │
│    · Complaint rate case       open → released (review.wrong)    │
│    · mail.acme-example.com     disabled → sending                │
│                                                                  │
│                                       [Save Assessment again]    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The commit failed on `UNIQUE (teamId, version)`. Nothing was written. The reviewer sees the event that arrived, a fresh preview, and decides again.

sections.title: v1 schema
sections.body:
```prisma
/// Append-only. The only source of truth for enforcement.
model EnforcementEvent {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  teamId      String                       // no FK cascade: the ledger outlives the team
  version     Int
  caseId      String                       // = id of the case's "opened" event
  type        String                       // zod-checked in append()
  data        Json
  actorUserId String?
  actorRule   String?                      // "health.complaint_rate@3", "legacy@backfill"
  note        String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([teamId, version])
  @@index([caseId, version])
}

/// Projection: one row per case. Written only by append().
model Enforcement {
  id              String    @id
  teamId          String
  sendingDomainId String?                   // null = whole team
  findingKey      String
  reason          String
  severityRank    Int
  status          String                    // open | released
  reviewedAt      DateTime?                 // last upheld
  openedAt        DateTime
  openedByUserId  String?
  openedByRule    String?
  closedAt        DateTime?
  closeReason     String?
  closedByUserId  String?
  version         Int

  @@index([teamId, status])
}
```

```sql
ALTER TABLE "EnforcementEvent" ADD CONSTRAINT actor_one
  CHECK (num_nonnulls("actorUserId", "actorRule") = 1);
ALTER TABLE "EnforcementEvent" ADD CONSTRAINT person_writes_note
  CHECK ("actorUserId" IS NULL OR btrim(coalesce(note, '')) <> '');

CREATE FUNCTION enforcement_event_append_only() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'EnforcementEvent is append-only (%)', TG_OP;
END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER enforcement_event_no_update BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON "EnforcementEvent"
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforcement_event_append_only();
CREATE TRIGGER enforcement_event_no_truncate BEFORE TRUNCATE ON "EnforcementEvent"
  FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION enforcement_event_append_only();

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX enforcement_open_finding ON "Enforcement" ("teamId", "findingKey") WHERE status = 'open';
CREATE INDEX enforcement_open_by_domain ON "Enforcement" ("sendingDomainId") WHERE status = 'open';
```

Owner consistency (a case's domain belongs to its team) is checked in `append()` validation in v1; a composite FK can follow.

sections.title: Later, without migrating data
sections.body:
| Later | How it arrives |
|---|---|
| Claiming, escalation, narrowing, corrections | new event types: one zod schema + one `apply` case |
| Exceptions (replaces `skipSafetyChecks`) | `allowed {target, findingKey?, until}`; `isAllowed(state, finding, at)` reads the clock, `apply` doesn't |
| Hold one email or one publish | `opened` payload gains `emailMessageId` / `effect`; `Enforcement` gains nullable columns |
| Second reviewer for high severity | a new `release_approved` event; existing `released` events keep their meaning |
| Shadow detectors | `proposed` events; the fold ignores them for `disabled` |
| Scorecard, time-to-review, reversal rate | folds over the ledger, back-filled by one replay |
| DB guard on `disabled` | a trigger rejecting writes not flagged by `append()`, once replay shows zero drift |
| Notifications to the team | a subscriber reading events by version |

sections.title: The v1 forest
sections.body:
> Main already funnels every disable through `models/sending-domain.ts`. Branches 1–7 are built and their tests pass locally; 8–10 and the gates are next. Nothing is pushed.

```
domain-enforcement → main, in merge order
1  feat(loo-6239): add the enforcement ledger                    built
   2  feat(loo-6239): add enforcement case queries               built  ↳ builds on 1
   3  feat(loo-6239): fold enforcement events                    built  ↳ builds on 1
      4  feat(loo-6239): preview and commit enforcement          built  ↳ builds on 3, requires 2
         5  feat(loo-6239): open a case for every disable        built  ↳ builds on 4
            6  feat(loo-6239): release cases on reenable         built  ↳ builds on 5
            7  feat(loo-6239): open legacy enforcement cases     built  ↳ builds on 5
            8  feat(loo-6239): replay enforcement nightly        next   ↳ builds on 5
               9  feat(loo-6239): preview domain assessments     next   ↳ builds on 6
                  10 feat(loo-6239): show reasons on domain review  next ↳ builds on 9
```

| # | What it does | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | insert-only ledger, version per team, team lock, actor CHECKs | query tests: UPDATE/DELETE raise, duplicate version fails, detector can't review, second writer waits |
| 2 | case + domain-flag projection queries | query tests |
| 3 | pure fold, 5 event types | event-list tests |
| 4 | `plan` shared by preview and commit; adoption of unexplained holds | model tests incl. "commit equals preview", "unexplained hold survives releasing a newer case" |
| 5 | all 16 disabling entry points pass a reason and an actor | real-DB smoke: 2 concurrent writers → versions 1–4, adoption, idempotent re-open |
| 6 | reenable releases cases; email override releases only its own | model tests with the real `plan` |
| 7 | `openLegacyEnforcementCases` script (dry run previews) | script tests |

No deploy-order edge is needed any more: adoption inside every commit means 6 is safe before 7 has run; 7 only fills the queue and reasons for domains nobody touches.

sections.title: Decisions for Phil
sections.body:
Codex's second review, against its 39 message-override cases, changed four things already (built): the team lock, version-before-cases reads, adoption of unexplained holds inside every commit, and the CHECK that only openings come from detectors. These are yours:

1. **Notes in a side table.** Codex: reviewers will paste support messages and contact details; an append-only note can't be redacted. A `EnforcementNote(eventId, body, redactedAt)` table keeps the ledger immutable and the text redactable. Built today: notes inline. **I'd follow Codex** — cheap now, painful after prod.
2. **Unleash as a ledger event.** Today Unleash sets `Team.skipSafetyChecks` outside the ledger, so the ledger can't say why later checks were skipped. Codex: record it as an event now (`allowed`, no expiry yet). I'd do it in a branch after v1.
3. **Release reason on Reenable.** Built: Reenable records `review.wrong`. The panel should let the reviewer pick wrong / fixed / released, so a sender's fix doesn't count against the detector.
4. **Email override no longer re-enables blindly.** Built: overriding one email releases that email's case and any unexplained legacy hold, and leaves the domain disabled if another reason (say a complaint rate) holds. That's the M004 fix, and a visible change for admins: the panel has to say why the domain stayed disabled.

Not covered by v1 and named honestly: all 39 overrides also grant a message exception, which v1 has no event for (Codex: `legacy.message_override_recorded` for history, `allowed` with email scope for the future).
